subject: NovaBank — Integration & Dedicated capacity ops playbook

Subject: NovaBank — integration & dedicated capacity follow-ups (post-demo)

Hi Samantha / Kevin —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can scope the Dedicated capacity proposal and the technical workshop:

High-level use cases we covered
- Customer support summarization + tool-call to fetch account details (low latency, per-request lookups)
- Enterprise search over internal docs with embeddings + reranker
- Transactional conversational assistant (multi-turn, long context)

Integration / architecture items we need to confirm
1) SDK & auth
   - Which auth flow do you prefer for server-side calls: API key/service account vs SAML-backed OAuth2 (SSO)? Any constraints (e.g., central IT policy that requires SAML)?
   - Do you want the SDK bundled in your build, or to proxy calls through your central inference gateway?
2) Routing & models
   - Will you enforce region pinning (US-only) for regulated PII workloads?
   - For the reranker/embeddings path, do you expect separate routing (embedding pool vs gen pool) or a unified pool?
3) Structured output / tool calling
   - Two patterns we recommend: 1) structured JSON outputs with Redwood's schema enforcement, 2) tool-calls for live lookups. Which is higher priority?
4) Embeddings & reranker scale
   - Ballpark index size and QPS (see bullets below) so we can size index-serving and memory needs.

Dedicated capacity sizing inputs we need from you
- Expected sustained queries/sec (inference requests) and expected peak burst (rps)
- Average prompt + response token length (tokens in/out) and percent of requests that use embeddings/reranker
- Concurrency target (how many simultaneous sessions you want to keep warm)
- Latency SLO (p50/p95 targets) and whether 95th-percentile latency > 300ms is acceptable for some flows

What I’ve attached
- novabank_requirements.xlsx (fill-in sheet for the fields above)
- redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf (SDK initialization & auth examples)

Immediate next steps
- Samantha: can you populate the sizing sheet by EOD Thu so Aditya and I can draft a Dedicated pool sizing + cost estimate?
- We'll schedule a 60–90 min technical workshop (Dev + infra) next week to walk through authentication, routing, and workspace-level isolation.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: NovaBank — integration & dedicated capacity follow-ups (post-demo)

Thanks, Priya — great summary. Answering inline against the asks and attaching the filled sizing tab: novabank_requirements_filled.xlsx.

Integration / architecture answers
- Auth: We need SAML-backed SSO for admin/control-plane (IAM), and server-to-server calls should use short-lived service account tokens. Corporate policy requires SSO for UIs; server keys are allowed but rotated monthly.
- SDK vs Gateway: We will proxy all outbound LLM calls through an internal inference gateway for auditing and traffic shaping. We'd still like the SDK for local dev and testing.
- Region: US-only for PII flows; non-PII dev workloads can be in EU.
- Routing: Prefer separate pools for embeddings (search) and generation to avoid contention.
- Structured output vs tool-calling: prioritized in this order: 1) schema-enforced structured JSON (for transactionality), 2) tool-call orchestration for back-office lookups.

Traffic & performance (estimates)
- Sustained requests: 80 rps gen requests (avg) with 150-token average response (100 tokens in, 150 out).
- Peak burst: up to 220 rps sustained for 5–10 minute windows during batch reconciliation jobs.
- Embeddings: 3k qps for vector inserts/queries over the first year; index size ~30M vectors (1536-d).
- Concurrency: target 45 concurrent sessions for the chat assistant with KV cache reuse expected to reduce compute by ~25%.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 350ms for the chat assistant; embeddings queries can be 500–800ms.

Compliance & security
- SOC2 required; we will share a vendor questionnaire if helpful.
- SSO setup will require a SAML metadata file and an SP connection.

We’ve attached the filled sheet and a short SSO scope doc: novabank_sso_sow.docx. Add Aditya to the workshop — he’ll own the infra requirements.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of AI Integrations | NovaBank

Subject: Re: NovaBank — integration & dedicated capacity follow-ups (post-demo)

Thanks for the numbers, Samantha — helpful. I sketched a practical Dedicated pool + routing approach below and a quick sizing back-of-envelope you can use to validate. We can go through this in the workshop and iterate.

Recommended deployment topology
- Two Dedicated pools: 1) gen-pool for conversation & structured outputs; 2) embed-pool for vector generation and search serving. Separate pools avoid noisy-neighbor effects and let us tune quantization independently.
- A small control-plane VM (private) that handles SAML SP, user provisioning, and proxies service-account token minting for server-to-server flows.
- Inference gateway: NovaBank's gateway will proxy to Redwood endpoints; we'll provide a short-lived signed-token flow + signature verification to let gateway assert the customer and route to the correct pool.

Autoscaling & concurrency
- Autoscale policy (suggested): gen-pool min=3 nodes, target=6 nodes, max=12 nodes. embed-pool min=1 node, target=2 nodes, max=4 nodes.
- Concurrency: set per-node concurrency limit to 24 concurrent streams for gen models (based on average 150-token responses). That yields ~144 concurrent sessions at target=6 nodes.
- Queueing: use per-customer request queues with dynamic priority. Max queue wait target 500ms; fallback policy routes non-critical long-running jobs to lower-cost burst tier.

Throughput math (approx)
- Given your numbers: 80 rps average * avg 250 tokens total (in + out) = 20k tokens/sec sustained.
- A single H100-equivalent node (in our internal benchmarks) can sustain ~10k tokens/sec for the model profile you demoed with batching active. So target=3 nodes to cover sustained (20k / 10k ≈ 2) with headroom => min 3, target 6 to hit peak bursts and failover.
- Peak 220 rps -> 55k tokens/sec -> requires ~6 H100-equivalent nodes with aggressive batching and warm KV cache; with max=12 you have headroom for growth.

Embeddings sizing
- For 30M vectors (1536-d) we recommend a dedicated index-serving fleet with 2 x A100-equivalent nodes for hot queries and an archival tier for cold shards.
- QPS 3k: tune index replicas and use short-lived caches for the top-k hot subsets.

Operational notes
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for conversational flows to cut redundant decoding cost (you noted many repeated system prompts).
- Quantization: test int8 for embedding generation; for gen models we recommend mixed-precision until we validate quality regressions.
- Monitoring: Redwood Console will expose model-level token breakdown, per-route P95 latency, and queue-depth alerts.

Deliverables before workshop
- Redwood will produce a 1-page Dedicated sizing sheet (node counts, autoscale policy, cost range) and an SDK + proxy integration checklist.
- I’ll include a short example of the short-lived token exchange and a sample SAML metadata consumer config.

Tagging items for the workshop: SSO SAML handoff (Evelyn), gateway token exchange (Aditya), embedding index layout (Monica).

—Aditya
